page: Amazon Web Services c7i-flex.8xlarge is a compute-optimized virtual server powered by the Nitro hypervisor. It features an x86_64 architecture with an Intel Xeon 8488C processor running at 3.2 GHz. The instance provides 32 vCPUs across 16 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled, alongside 64.0 GB of DDR5 memory operating at 5 GHz. This configuration yields a 1:2 vCPU-to-RAM ratio, allocating 2.0 GB of memory per core. The processor includes an L3 cache of 105 MB, L2 cache of 2 MB, and L1d cache of 48 KB. It lacks local storage and dedicated GPU hardware, relying on external network-attached storage, and delivers a baseline network bandwidth of 6 Gbps.

Performance benchmarks indicate strong single-core and multi-core capabilities. The server achieves a Geekbench single-core score of 2074.0 and a multi-core score of 15951.0, both placing in the top 25% tier. Single-threaded gzip compression reaches 33.6 GB/sec, and single-threaded bzip3 decompression performs at 13.85 GB/sec, both demonstrating high efficiency in data serialization tasks. In cryptographic workloads, the Passmark CPU encryption test scores 35678.6, supported by hardware-accelerated instruction sets such as AES and VAES. Additionally, static web serving throughput is measured at 51.12 GB/sec, highlighting its efficiency in high-concurrency web delivery.

The hardware supports advanced vector and matrix extensions, including AVX-512 and Intel AMX (Advanced Matrix Extensions) for deep learning and integer operations. This is reflected in LLM inference benchmarks, where text generation using a small 135M model reaches 286.26 tokens/sec, and prompt processing for a medium 7B model achieves 150.07 tokens/sec. From a cost-efficiency perspective, the flex designation represents a resource-dense compute option that balances high-frequency Intel Xeon processing with a moderate memory footprint, making it a viable alternative to standard compute-optimized instances for workloads that do not require continuous maximum CPU utilization. Appropriate workloads include static web serving, software compilation, medium-scale database operations, and text-based machine learning inference.
